fit: Lewy body dementia case with formed visual symptoms
assessment: Conference member subarticle832 distinguishes visual hallucinations and clinical parkinsonism in a Lewy body dementia case. The diagnosis and case trajectory do not give repeated visual episodes after fig consumption.

fit: amantadine switch and hallucination adverse event
assessment: An open-label subgroup of 24 Parkinson deep brain stimulation patients switched from immediate-release to extended-release amantadine. The report gives hallucination adverse events in 25% and contains no separate count of visual episodes. NCT02202551 is the parent study.

fit: visual hallucinations and place misidentification in dementia
assessment: The Lewy body dementia case describes visual hallucinations as well as a separate misidentification delusion and cognitive fluctuations. It lacks a timed food comparison or count of visual episodes.

fit: inhaled levodopa safety and occurrence of hallucination
assessment: Short studies report hallucination adverse-event participants in 1.5% with inhaled levodopa versus 1.3% with placebo. The longer study includes a nonrandom observational comparison, 2.2% versus 1.6%. A visual hallucination appears among treatment discontinuation reasons. These figures are participants with events and no food was compared.

fit: pimavanserin chart review and global clinical impressions
assessment: Six medicated patients included four with Parkinson disease and two with dementia with Lewy bodies. The chart review reports an overall improvement in the hallucinations and delusions clinical impression at three months. It gives no comparator or separate visual episode rate.

fit: visual hallucination presence and future dementia in a prodromal cohort
assessment: Visual hallucinations were present in 37 of 73 participants with MCI and Lewy body features. The clinical features informed selection. Follow-up analyzed conversion to dementia. Presence and time to dementia are distinct from food-linked visual episode frequency.

fit: family history and clinical phenotype in Lewy body dementia
assessment: The retrospective comparison uses family history, first symptom and longitudinal cognition in 154 familial and 137 sporadic participants. It provides diagnostic and biomarker context without a separately assigned dried fig exposure.

fit: food frequency categories and fecal microbiome comparison
assessment: The dietary table lists seventeen food and beverage categories without figs or a fruit intake item. The analysis compares fecal taxa with diagnosis and sleep phenotype. Visual hallucinations appear in disease background, with no exposure-timed episode outcome.

fit: multisensory hallucination categories and functional brain connectivity
assessment: The full preprint analyzes 53 people with Parkinson disease and differentiates minor, structured and absent hallucination groups. Structured symptoms combine visual, auditory and other modalities. The model and induced sensed-presence task do not measure dried fig intake or separately count visual episodes after exposure.

fit: high nutmeg use and insomnia in a non-Parkinson mania case
assessment: Clinicians report mixed insomnia and auditory hallucinations during acute mania after unusually high nutmeg use. Culinary preparation, route, dose and baseline insomnia severity are unspecified. The timing, concurrent syndrome and later drug treatment cannot isolate a ground nutmeg effect. Preserve this adverse-use case alongside the reported powdered nutmeg and milk insomnia observation.
